   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Phil Glover SAM ADVENTURE
      CLUB, 43, Ferndale Road,
      Hall Green, BIRMINGHAM,
      West Midlands  B28 9AU

We'll be increasing the price of
the disk from Issue 8 onwards
and charging a small membership
fee. When we started the club we
hoped to keep the price down as
low as possible but postal costs
in particular have piled up.
Mailing the disks isn't too bad
but we have to keep in regular
touch with software publishers,
other SAM disk mags and advent-
ure mags, write to members, and
many other people. Also, review
disks to other magazines have to
be paid for out of our own pock-
ets, so our finances are far
from healthy!

Issue 8 onwards will cost `2.50
and club membership for one year
will be `1.00. To soften the
blow, we'll offer three disks
and year's free membership for
`7.00. We don't want members to
order more than three disks in
advance at present, as we can't
know for sure how the club will
be doing in six month's time. If
disaster strikes, we'd like to
be sure of giving full refunds
to everyone. At the moment the
future looks bright and we think
the club will continue to grow,
with your continued support.

Sorry if you think that the
price increase is a bit steep,
but we consider it is essential
if we're to keep the club
functioning well.

       Good adventuring,

          Phil Glover

P.S. Congratulations on OUTWRITE
2; it's superb and I'll leave my
copy of THE SECRETARY to gather
dust!

From: Cliff Jackson, SOUTHAMPTON

Dear Ron and Brian,,

"TIME-CHECK" for MDOS and SAMBus

I found that the clock within my
SAMBus was not at all accurate
over a period. I mentioned this
when I last wrote to Alan Miles
just before the crash, but of
course have received no reply.

I, therefore, removed the case
and found on the pcb a small
varicap, adjustment of which
over a fortnight or so has
achieved reasonable accuracy
(gain of 1 second in 3 days)
although, over a longer period,
I hope to do even better.

I have on my desk a small calc-
ulator with a built-in digital
clock that I use as my reference
for all domestic timekeeping. I
am usually quite methodical when
adjusting digital clocks (of
which I've had some experience)
but I got into a bit of a muddle
when writing down dates and time
differences when first attempt-
ing to adjust the clock in the
'bus.

I decided that SAM should be
able to help here and so "TIME
CHECK" was devised to record in
an array the true time (which I
Input) plus SAM time and the
date (up to 30 times).

[TIME-CHECK is in this month's
OUTLET - BC]

I found that running the program
regularly is a very easy way of
keeping track of the effective-
ness of the adjustments made to
the clock -the "filled" elements
of the array are printed on
screen after each "run" and the
counter is incremented before
the program is SAVEd "Over" so
that when re-LOADed the program
automatically fills the next
free element. The whole array is
then displayed together with the
time difference.


I've added a bit of text to give
readers some general guidance on
adjusting the SAMBus clock which
is quite straightforward.

Incidentally, I strongly reject
Alan Cox's views on the exclus-
ion of programs using MDos/BASIC
and feel obliged to respond to
his comments.

My view is that the use of these
programs should be encouraged to
the point that programs which
will not run when MD or MB are
resident should be regarded as
not fully-compatible. I under-
stand that this problem is
caused by the programmer having
ignored SAMCo's guide-lines on
the use of the "Heap" - but I
believe that even SAMCo flouted
their own rules occasionally.

Surely it would be far better if
MDos with MBASIC was to become
the standard, so making SAM an

even more elegant machine than
the basic unit with SAMDOS
alone. Indeed, I tend to use the
combined MDos+MBAS for all pur-
poses and only resort to SAMDOS
when forced by the program being
run. The loss in that situation
of the excellent facilities
which Dr Andy Wright's magical
Dos extensions provide is quite
frustrating when (say) customis-
ing a program which breaks the
"Heap" rules.

Surely, anyone without these
superb programs cannot really be
serious about SAM? They ARE
available to all and at a very
modest price - perhaps the best
value-for-money in software any-
where. Surely we cannot expect
talented programmers to devote


their time to writing for our
machine if we publicly suggest
that potential buyers should
wait until their programs fall
into the public domain so that
we can get them for peanuts thus
robbing the author of his/her
very just but often quite modest
reward.For those who do not have
these programs, I say, "send off
for them now". Usual disclaimers
- I am just a fervent admirer of
Andy's talents(without which SAM
would not be the machine it is
today).

Nevertheless,I realise that  you
must make OUTLET compatible with
the  "basic"  machine  but  that
precaution  should  not  exclude
the use of, (and development  of
ideas to make  even  better  use


of), the  marvellous  additional
facilities which Andy's programs
bestow.

I was interested to read of Alan
Cox's conversion of a 128K
Spectrum Program to run on SAM.
Can we persuade him to write it
up for publication in OUTLET so
we can all learn something about
page-switching(on both machines)
- which I am sure many readers
would find most interesting and
informative.

Although this was written on
OUTWRITE 2 (which I already like
very much), I intend to print it
using a version of TASWORD 2 to
which I added a routine which
prints automatically in 2 x 32

columns (a bit like Dr. Mike
Haine's 2 colpr which prints in
2 x 64 cols) but only if the
right margin is set at 32 when
F9 is pressed in the printer
menu. I intend to have a go at
adding this to OUTWRITE 2 when
time permits.

        Yours sincerely,

          Cliff Jackson

Brian Cavers to Cliff Jackson

Regarding MASTERDOS and MASTER
BASIC, firstly, I have no plans
or intentions to exclude any
programs that specifically need
to use either or both. The only
exception might be that if I got
six or eight such programs sent
in at one time I'd certainly not
put them all in one issue! One
or two is quite alright but it
would be absurd to have a lot of
programs in OUTLET that will
only work with special software.
Supposing I publish all the text
in OUTWRITE format and insist
everybody buy OUTWRITE to read
it (even though I think OUTWRITE
is the standard SAM Coupe word
processor any anyone who has not
got it is missing out badly!

Secondly, as far standards go,
neither MD nor MB can be made
THE standard by proclamation or
desire - the standard IS SAMDOS
in the sense that everyone has
it and it can be included with
any software. I repeat again, I
dearly wish MD and MB WERE the
standard available to everyone -
but they are not.

Compatiblity with MD or MB is
NOT necessarily or even commonly
the fault of the other software.
If a piece of software needs to
use all the SAM's memory then it
cannot work if MB is grabbing an
extra page but at least you can
reset and reload with SAMDOS. If
a program relies on MB though,it
is tough luck.

Price: MD and MB together cost
almost `32. They may be good
value but so is a Porsche! Many
people out of work or on an old
age pension are struggling to
find an extra `5 for essentials
these days let alone luxuries.

I'm sorry if I sound a little
harsh on this matter of money
but I've spent most of my life
desparately struggling to make
ends meet and I still am! You
must not take it for granted
that anyone can just "send off
for them now" and anyone who
has not got them "cannot be
serious about SAM". I budget
around 60p per meal; `32 would
buy me a lot of dinners! Ee by
gum, times is hard, lad!

Nevertheless, I get your drift
and, like you, wish everyone had
MD and MB as standard.

As usual, don't take any notice
of my ravings -nothing personal!

This two-column routine you have
looks interesting. Why not send
it in if you do an OUTWRITE
version?If you make it mergeable
that is.

                       - Brian

From: Brian Lofkin, CREWE

Dear OUTLET,

In September I finally sent in
my standing order request for
OUTLET, after first filling it
in, in May.It was at that time I
was made redundant and the cost
of `3 per issue held me back. I
have now reached the state where
I am totally bored and  wanted
something extra to entertain me.

Reading the back issues 57-61
was to some extent depressing,
with all the talk of having to
take additional work, coupled
with the demise of SAM and the
"I told you so" brigade. (You
always get some, I suppose). For
me, any job would be a blessing!

Please note that if the OUTLET
price is increased I will term-
inate my subscription. I take
Fred and Format magazines which
cover the majority of my needs.
One method of paying for contri-
butions would be to give free
subscriptions to OUTLET - number
of issues dependant on the prog-
rams, rather than cash payment.

With regards to Alan Cox's
comments in OUTLET 61 about
MASTER Dos and BASIC, these
programs are too valuable to
consider not utilising their in-
creased versatility/power in
magazines or any programs. If
people want to live in the Dark
Ages that is their loss. These
programs put SAM in the 1990's

with an almost professional per-
formance; this limited only by
the quality of programs avail-
able. The sooner they are sold
with all new SAMs the better!

I have Personal Banking System
from Hilton.This is a profess-
ional piece of software. Using
SAMDOS2 it was painfully slow
and slipped out of BASIC on
numerous occasions. With MASTER
DOS-BASIC loaded it works so
much faster and I have not had
any problems in running it.

This letter is being written on
'SPELL MASTER' as it is the only
word processing package I
currently have. It is one of the
few programs that will not run

when MD-B are loaded - it
crashes. With SAMDOS2 it works
perfectly; within the limits it
sets itself.


The dictionary has some unusual
spellings, it does not recognise
"utilising"but does "utilizing".


The talk is that it has a lot of
American spellings but according
to my 1975 Oxford English Dict-
ionary "utilizing" is correct.
My 1985 Collins Concise English
Dictionary accepts both spell-
ings. Can anyone confirm that
the use of z instead of s is
correct English or Americanese?

What are the main differences
between 'STYLE WRITER' and
'OUTWRITE!'I want a fully
operational word processing
package for my own personal use.
That way I can send letters for
jobs etc.

Are there any printers which can
be recommended from personal
use?

The 'Shorely Not' program in
OUTLET 61 highlighted a problem
I have seen occasionally with
some OUTLET programs. Whilst
perusing the BASIC listing the
curser locks up after line 9986.
Line 9 is there with a jumble of
?? and copyright symbols. (the
copyright symbol does not type
in on SPELL MASTER).

On pressing the reset button and
ENTER the listing goes from 9984
to 59800, with no line 9.Is this
caused by something added to the
program or a fault with my comp-
uter? Brian Gaff knows I have a
problem but we have been unable
to identify the cause. If this
is not a program feature, it may
help sort out my computer.

              TTFN,

             Brian

Brian Cavers to Brian Lofkin

I've answered the comments about
MASTERDOS and MASTERBASIC in my
reply to Cliff Jackson and can
only re-affirm, yes, yes, yes, I
wish they were the standard but
because not everyone has them it
would not be fair to have large
numbers of programs in OUTLET
that rely on them to work - nor
to reject programs that crash if
they are present. I think that
the mouse should be standard but
it would be unfair to restrict
many of our programs to using it
when many do not have the mouse
or even want it.

Sorry to hear you will not be
buying OUTLET after the increase
in price next year.

There are numerous English words
with alternate spelling,possibly
due to American influence and I
am sure both utilize and utilise
are both correct. Where realized
(or realised!), I have tried to
put both in our OUTWRITE spell
dictionary.

You should by now have received
our info on STYLE WRITER and
OUTWRITER and will note that the
main original difference was
that STYLE WRITER could include
graphics - although slower than
OUTWRITE. Version 2 of OUTWRITE
now has many more features which
can be seen in our ADD-VERT.

Line 9986 has UDGs hidden in the
line which crash if edited.

You will note that many programs
have what seems to be a huge
line 9965 (but which is really
just a few TAB commands). This
line helps to buffer the effect
of line 9986 when editing above
but scrolling up and down thru'
line 9986 is likely to crash it.

The advantage of such lines (see
also line 9994 which has our
standard character set creator:
AUTOCHARS) is it is easier to
copy the main program if you do
not need to copy other files as
well and it speeds up loading.

This is a practice carried over
from the Spectrum whose BASIC is
much more stable in this respect
and more tolerant.

You can easily pass line 9986
and 9994 by just clearing the
screen and entering LIST 9995.

                        - Brian

From: S.M. Goodman, LEEDS

Dear Brian, Ron, and Averil,

Thanks once more for another
enjoyable OUTLET (Issue 62). I
echo the support offered by
other readers who feel that a
price rise would not be unreas-
onable. After all, one normally
looks forward to a pay increase
each year, and you should not be
excepted.

It's nice to see my "variables"
puzzle has had a response with
one or two elegant ideas, which
make my solution, (with you),
rather long-winded. Most solut-
ions seem to concentrate on pro-
cessing a given strong variable,

whereas my answer offers a num-
eric/string approach.Still, it's
good to see people rise to a
challenge. What a pity Sinclair
didn't provide for'long' strings
such as CHARLIE$ or help etc.
Had he done so the problem would
never (?) have arisen.

I went to the local All Formats
Fair here in Leeds last Sunday.
The hall was half empty and
apart from the 'Format' stand,
which appeared to be doing very
little whilst I was there, there
was no Spectrum/SAM support.

I met Bruce Everiss, briefly,
whilst he was dishing  out his
'`1.00 off' vouchers, which gave
me a chance to tell hilm that I
thought his admission price was

too high. However, I did find a
table where advance tickets
could be bought for `2.00 which
I feel is on the upper limit of
a realistic price.

Now onto a suggestion. As I
mentioned earlier. there was
little support for our 8 bit
machines and I wondered if there
was any mileage in approaching
the other regular 8 bit mag-
azines (Enceladus, Fred, Sam
Supplement, Format) to take a
stand on a cost-sharing basis,
so that your 'presence' wouuld
only cost `10 to `15 per show
instead of `60. So, you could be
present at Leicester with the
others products, someone else in
Scotland, and so on - and with
that thought I will close.

         Best Regards,

  Malcolm 'The Poser' Goodman

P.S. Hope you've got a good
solution!!

P.P.S. A use for VAL$ ?? (or
have I missed the point?)...

 5 LET a = 10: LET a$ = "hello"
10 LET b$ = "a$  AND a  = 10"
20 PRINT VAL$ b$.

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Goodman

It's about time I published your
own solution to your puzzle; it
is in this month's ADD-ENDERS. I
do not know at this moment if it
will work/convert on SAM as it
modifies the BASIC itself with a
system variable but if so I will
put it in the SAM version too -
even though KEYIN would do the
same. If it's not there you know
it wouldn't convert!

You idea of sharing the costs of
an ALL-FORMATS stand is a good
one.Some of us have already done
sharing at various times; it is
one of these variable things
that happens from time to time
in different ways.

Your use of VAL$ is correct but
if you look closely you are
really just adding the extra
bits unnecessarily. If you strip
the quotes from line 10 and the
VAL$ from line 20, it does the
same thing...

 5 LET a=10: LET a$="hello"
10 LET b$=a$ AND a=10
20 PRINT b$

I've found this myself whenever
I thought I'd invented a genuine
use for VAL$ it always turned
out to be an unnecessary extra.

Can anyone else think of a real
use for VAL$ that is genuinely
the "best" programming method in
a particular situation?
                        - Brian

From: E. Thomson, Suffolk



Dear Chezron,

Two things: Malcolm Goodman's
problem (Spectrum program) and
the "EASTER" calculator.

I use INPUT x$ to specify the
variable whose value is to be
given, so the already stored x$
must be copied somewhere. Since
Spectrum BASIC allows only one-
letter names for strings and
string arrays, and the name of a
string array can't be the same
as a string variable, the only
way I can think of is to use a
numerical array; it must have a

one-letter name, but this can be
the same as that of a numerical
variable.

I have to use a counting vari-
able, n, so the "real" value of
n must also be copied.


The routine proper starts at
Line 100, and, theoretically,
the variables a,b,...,z and
a$,b$,...,z$ have been given
values previously; the program
gives values to a few, so that
the routine can be tested.


[the program listed on the next
page is on the SAM OUTLET disc
in ADD-ENDERS as"MGPROBLEM" -Ed]

10 LET a=1:LET b=2:LET n=14: LET
   x=24
20 LET a$="alpha":LET b$="bravo"
   :Let x$="x-ray"
100 DIM n(2): LET n(1)=n: LET
    n(2)=LEN x$
110 DIM x(n(2))
120 FOR n=1 TO n(2):
    LET x(n)=CODE x$(n): NEXT n
130 INPUT "variable name:";x$
140 PRINT x$;":";
150 IF LEN x$=2 THEN GO TO 190
160 IF x$="n" THEN PRINT n(1)
170 IF x$<>"n" THEN PRINT VAL x$
180 GO TO 210
190IF x$<>"x$"THEN PRINT VAL$ x$
200 IF x$="x$" THEN GO SUB 300:
    PRINT x$
210 GO TO 130
300 LET x$="": FOR n=1 TO n(2)
310 LET x$=x$+CHR$ x(n): NEXT n
320 RETURN

In Alan Cox's program for calc-
ulating Easter (OUTLET 61, "More
Mail"), the year has to be 1583
onwards, which must be because
of the new calendar system
introduced by Pope Gregory in
October 1582, when 10 days were
"lost". This Gregorian system
was presumably adopted by Roman
Catholic countries, but not
everywhere. Britain did not
adopt it until September 1752,
when 11 days were lost, and
Russia waited until 1919. So if
you use this program for calc-
ulating Easter in Britain, a
year before 1753 would give the
wrong answer.
              Regards,

          Ettrick Thomson

From: Alan D. Cox. DYFED

Dear Brian,

Thank you for Issue 62(excellent
as ever), for publishing LETTA
CHECKA, and for the comment that
it inspired the SPELL CHECKER in
OUTWRITE! v.2. It is the first
time that one of my programs has
inspired anything other than
rage for me when one did not
work!

I think your comment on the
first page may slightly mislead
people - LETTA CHECKA does not
care about the end of a line,
only about the end of a word,
and in this role it recognises a
space and all the (more obvious)
punctuation marks.

The reason it does not work with
e.g., TASWORD is that the latter
does not record an explicit end-
of-word marker when a word ends
at the end of a line: I imagine
it uses its internal knowledge
of line length instead.

        All best wishes

          Alan D. Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan Cox



Because LETTA CHECKA was used
with WM, I think I jumped to the
conclusion it would regard a
code 13 in the same way as a
space - i.e., it would mark the
end of a word, but that a 10
line feed as well (some word
processors have both) might
confuse it (e.g., if it merely
incremented past the 13). I do
not think I gave it enough
thought actually else I could
have tested it with a dummy file
(I don't actually know of any
SAM wordprocessor files that use
both a 13 and a 10 but some CP/M
ones might).

Regarding your query about the
upgrade to OUTWRITE 2, yes,
just send your Version 1 disc
and the `3 fee.
                         - Brian

From: Mervyn Toogood, BRISTOL


Dear Brian,

I have written to a couple of
various clubs for help before I
became a member of OUTLET but
"no joy" in reference to a
reply. I feel sure it will not
happen when writing to you.

I have a Spectrum +3 and Epson
LX-400 printer. Can I get a
printout of the contents page,
and how?

Thanking you in anticipation.

        Mervyn Toogood

Brian Cavers to Mervyn Toogood

To print a copy of the OUTLET
CONTENTS page on the +3 version:

1. RESET

2. Enter MERGE "CONTENTS"

3. Wait a few seconds until
   "O.K." appears.

4. Press the ENTER key.

5. Type: 26 COPY then press
   the ENTER key.

6. Type: RUN then press ENTER.

Disciple/+D users load the usual
way; use SAVE SCREEN$ instead of
COPY (or the snap button).

SAM users should first load the
DUMP code or MASTERBASIC and
then use DUMP instead of COPY.

Other users will need their own
dump software. If you enter...

     SAVE "CONSCRN" SCREEN$

       ...at line 26 then you
could save the CONTENTS screen
and load it into any program
that will print a screen.

                       - Brian.

Я решил, что SAM вполне способен помочь в этом деле, и придумал «TIME-CHECK», чтобы записывать в массив точное время (которое я ввожу с клавиатуры), плюс время SAM и дату (до 30 записей).

Затем весь массив выводится на экран вместе с разницей во времени.

Я добавил немного текста, чтобы дать читателям общее руководство по настройке часов SAMBus, что на самом деле довольно просто.

Чтобы распечатать копию страницы СОДЕРЖАНИЯ (CONTENTS) OUTLET на версии для +3:

4. Нажмите клавишу ENTER.
5. Наберите: `26 COPY` и нажмите клавишу ENTER.

Пользователи Disciple/+D загружают программу обычным способом; вместо COPY используйте SAVE SCREEN$ (или кнопку сброса дампа/снапшота).

